question: As per the Sustainable Development Goals – National Indicator Framework Progress Report, 2025, population covered by social protection systems has increased to which level in 2025, indicating substantial expansion in social security coverage in the country?
solution:
The correct answer is __**64.3%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sustainable Development Goals – National Indicator Framework (NIF) Progress Report, 2025**, released by the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**, provides a comprehensive overview of India’s progress toward the **2030 Agenda**.
 
• According to the **2025** report, the percentage of the population covered by **social protection systems** or floors has seen a substantial increase, reaching **64.3%**.
 
• This indicator is specifically linked to **SDG Target 1.3**, which focuses on implementing nationally appropriate social protection systems and measures for all, including floors, to achieve substantial coverage of the poor and the vulnerable.
 
• The expansion to **64.3%** reflects the successful scaling of various **government-led interventions** designed to provide a safety net against economic and social risks.
 
• The **National Indicator Framework (NIF)** serves as the backbone for monitoring **SDGs** in India, currently tracking **284 indicators** across all **17 Sustainable Development Goals**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Social Protection Systems:**
 
 
• These systems encompass a set of policies and programs designed to reduce **poverty** and vulnerability by promoting efficient labour markets and enhancing the capacity of individuals to manage risks such as **sickness**, **disability**, **unemployment**, and **old age**.
 
• In India, this includes major schemes such as the **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)**, **PM-KISAN**, and various **pension schemes** for the elderly and widowed.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goal 1 (No Poverty):**
 
 
• **SDG 1** aims to end poverty in all its forms everywhere. **Indicator 1.3.1** specifically tracks the proportion of the population covered by social protection floors/systems, disaggregated by sex and key vulnerable groups.
 
• The **2025 report** indicates that India is moving closer to its targets through **digital transformation** and **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** mechanisms.
 
 
 
• **Role of MoSPI:**
 
 
• The **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)** is the nodal agency for the **Sustainable Development Goals** indicators in India.
 
• It collaborates with various **Central Ministries** and **State Governments** to collect and validate data for the **National Indicator Framework**.
 
 
 
• **Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI):**
 
 
• The expansion of social security coverage to **64.3%** is largely attributed to the **JAM Trinity** (Jan Dhan, Aadhaar, and Mobile), which has streamlined the identification and delivery of benefits to the **unorganized sector**.
 
• The **e-Shram portal** has also played a pivotal role in registering over **29 crore unorganized workers**, facilitating their inclusion into the national social security net.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Target 1.3 Implementation:** India’s approach to social protection is multi-layered, covering **health insurance** through **Ayushman Bharat**, **life insurance** through **PMJJBY**, and **accidental insurance** through **PMSBY**.
 
• **Impact of the 2025 Report:** The report serves as a critical tool for **policy makers** to identify gaps in service delivery and re-allocate resources to states or sectors that are lagging in **social security** reach.
 
• **Global Comparison:** The increase to **64.3%** positions India as a leader among developing nations in terms of the rapid scale-up of **social safety floors** within a decade.
 
• **Future Projections:** The government aims to achieve near-universal coverage by **2030**, focusing on the **gig economy** and **migrant laborers** who were previously outside the formal social protection ambit.

87:T
